text: This Act will regulate kindergartens and childcare centres under the same framework to ensure higher and more consistent standards across the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: ECDA has consulted parents and the sector extensively.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Overall, there has been strong support to better safeguard our children's interests and to raise the quality of services rendered.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: ECDA has received many useful feedback and suggestions and we will take them into consideration.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Committed and passionate educators, clearly, are the foundation of our early childhood sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We agree with Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Sun Xueling that we need sufficient manpower to support our ramp-up in childcare capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To attract more educators, we have introduced training awards and scholarships for ITE and Polytechnic diploma students.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have also enhanced professional conversion programmes for mid-career entrants.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: A new Place-and-Train Programme for educarers was introduced last year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have expanded continuing professional development opportunities to develop and retain educators in the sector and this is an important effort.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Late last year, I launched the Professional Development Programme to help teachers deepen their competencies and to take on larger job roles.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Over 100 teachers are in the first batch and I expect many more to benefit in future runs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are also building a pipeline of preschool teachers to support children with mild development needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Ngee Ann Polytechnic will offer a Specialist Diploma in Early Childhood Learning Support from April this year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The manpower situation for this sector will remain tight.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: ECDA will continue to study how to make it easier for those with the passion to work with young children to join the sector, while continuing to assure parents that the safety and welfare of our children are looked after.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We do want to ensure preschool remains affordable to families, a point raised by Members Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To achieve this, we have done two things.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Today, over 40% of Singaporean children are enrolled in childcare centres under these schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is a significant increase from 20% in 2012.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And in the next few years, we will reach 50%.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The schemes have helped to moderate fee increases.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Similarly, kindergartens run by MOE and Anchor Operators are also widely accessible, comprising about half of all kindergartens.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For kindergartens, our means-tested KiFAS subsidies are targeted at these operators to support lower- and middle-income parents with the cost.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Beyond these broad-based measures, it is important to do more for vulnerable children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There is a small group of parents who do need support to give their children a good start.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There are many reasons why families and parents may end up in those situations.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Page: 105 We all know that a strong parent-child relationship is key in the development of the child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But when the relationship has broken down and the child has to be temporarily separated from the parent, we must do what we can to rebuild and to reunify the relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I will explain how we translate this principle into practice.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When a marriage breaks down, children, more often than not, become the vulnerable party.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is especially important for parents to improve their parenting capacity and skills to prevent the parent-child relationship from breaking down and to take active steps to improve it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But we should not see the parent-child relationship break down.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We all know that in acrimonious divorces, sometimes, the children get dragged into the battle.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This will help them make an informed decision on divorce matters.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But if they were to proceed, hopefully, they proceed in an informed fashion so that they can work on a sustainable co-parenting plan, post-separation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This programme is one of the many divorce support programmes offered by the four MSF-appointed Divorce Support Specialist Agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Leon Perera talks about social mobility and it is important to measure it and to spur policy innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Indeed, Singapore is a very good example of how social mobility has benefited many of us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think for many of us in this House, our grandparents were not rich.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Yet, within a generation and a generation and a half, many of us in Singapore have been uplifted.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is not something that we ought to take for granted because, as society matures, as the economy matures, it does become more difficult and, in every society, Singapore included, there will be families and individuals who will find themselves in difficult circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have been monitoring our social mobility indicators.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: By and large, while there are different definitions and ways of looking at it, we have done relatively well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For the US, UK and Denmark, the shares are 8%, 9% and 12% respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The same study, which is an update of their study in 2012, also found that our mobility has remained fairly stable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While the findings are encouraging, what is more important is we need to understand what have we got right, what are the areas that we need to continue to improve and how do we sustain this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As I have mentioned, as we mature as an economy, as a society, it will become more difficult.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some children, possibly because of complex family circumstances, already lag behind developmentally even in their early years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Leon Perera talks about stories which his friends shared.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I can share with you more stories because we do see individuals, children, who have somehow not broken free from the cycle in which the parents find themselves in.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In order to help these children, we must go upstream and provide additional support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Dr Lily Neo and Mr Ang Hin Kee have illustrated some of the circumstances that these families face.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I think many of us in this House would have encountered individuals who face those difficulties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Page: 106 Today, we have a range of services to promote the health and learning needs of young children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is not meant to be a discrete programme; it is meant to be a holistic approach to intervening in these earlier years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Their parents may be unable to provide a supportive environment for a host of reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For example, they could be young, unwed or incarcerated.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There could be a combination of all these various factors, coupled with limited or no extended family support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These families would benefit and they do need additional help.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I am heartened to hear that many Members are supportive of this initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To implement KidSTART, ECDA will set up a Programme Office and work with Government agencies and selected SSOs, hospitals and community partners to identify, reach out to and provide coordinated support to these children and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Take, for example, a young, single, unwed, first-time mother with a three-month-old infant.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: She has gone to SSO for financial assistance as she is unemployed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As a first-time mother, while she wants the best for her child, she has limited knowledge, resources and, perhaps, not having the extended family support to nurture the child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Through KidSTART, this mother will be supported and, if possible, even as early as the antenatal stage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: During my recent visit to KK Hospital, a doctor told me how early intervention even at this stage is important for the development of the child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It could help the child to be brought to term healthily, at a good birth weight.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will continue to support the parent beyond this stage, with home visits, parent education, family support programmes and, depending on their needs, she may be linked up to support groups and existing community resources.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But she also has to play a part.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is where we endeavour to do as much as we can to reach out.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Through these, we will work with the parent to create a supportive and nurturing environment for the child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The parent may also be assisted to place the child in an affordable and good quality preschool or childcare centre, with the appropriate development programmes to make sure that they are receiving the right kind of exposure.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will start small and focus so that it allows us to make sure that we are able to help effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The intent is there and we need to do this well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I want this model to work because I want to be able to ramp up and help more children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Many of you here have spoken up for unwed parents – Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin, Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap, Ms K Thanaletchimi, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Dennis Tan, Mr Louis Ng and Mr Desmond Choo all talked about extending benefits, such as maternity leave and the CDA First Step to unwed parents and parity for all Singaporean children regardless of their parents' marital status.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I want to recognise Mr Seah Kian Peng, in particular, Page: 107 who has been urging the Ministry for a very long time to give more help to single parents, particularly, unwed parents and their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Before I address Members' concerns, I think it is important to say a few things.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: First, single parents are not, I repeat, are not, a uniform group.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Divorced and widowed single parents who form the bulk of single parents are already eligible for the same parenthood benefits as married parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Like all other children, children of unwed parents have access to social assistance, education and healthcare subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They are also eligible for infant care and childcare subsidies, MediSave grant for newborns and the foreign domestic worker levy concession, to date.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But I do understand where Members are coming from, which is why when I first joined MSF, I wanted to review this policy because I do meet unwed mothers, particularly when they come to see me at the Meet-the-People Sessions (MPS).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They are vulnerable usually, because they are younger and lower educated.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some may have been rejected by their own families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is difficult enough to bring up children, but to do so single-handedly, without family support, is really tough.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some may have hoped to have a child within marriage but, due to circumstances, ended up as unwed parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I feel that we can do more to support their efforts to care for their children and reduce the disadvantages that their children may face at birth.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In fact, as in the earlier example when I talked about KidSTART, I think the children of unwed mothers, especially those in the more vulnerable situation, will be those that we are reaching out to help.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will need to amend the legislation to make this happen and this should be able to come into effect for children born from early next year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are in the process of working on the legislation to get it in place, as well as the system enhancement; and this is likely to kick in for children born from the third quarter of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These benefits are useful in the child's developmental or caregiving needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They also support the unwed parent's efforts to provide for the child.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: At the same time, the extension of these benefits to unwed parents does not undermine parenthood within marriage, which is something that we do encourage and it is still the prevalent social norm.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These are the reasons behind this particular decision.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: On top of this, MSF and NCSS will also work with the relevant VWOs and agencies to strengthen support for families with vulnerable, low-income unwed mothers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is to enable them to make better-informed decisions to improve their financial and family stability and, ultimately, to enhance their child's outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng highlighted the concerns about children who are maltreated by their families or caregivers, especially those with special needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We have been working with the Page: 108 community to improve early detection and to better protect these children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Where needed, we provide a safe place and therapy to help them heal and recover.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This includes foster care which provides these children with a caring and stable family environment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are expanding our fostering capacity and have made encouraging progress.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We aim to recruit another 130, especially for older children and those with special needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Two fostering agencies were set up last year to support foster parents; providing parenting advice, counselling and connecting them to relevant community resources.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I do ask for your support to encourage more families to step forward to consider fostering.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Fostering is always a better option than institutional care for some of these children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Now, there are children with higher needs that will benefit from very intensive, very specialised care in smaller residential home settings.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The childhood trauma contributed to the challenging behaviours of these children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As far as possible, such out-of-home care should be temporary arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Where it is safe and possible, children should be reunited with their own families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We should also go upstream to strengthen the family and preserve the parent-child relationships, to prevent these children from being placed in alternative care in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Through this pilot, we hope to provide time-limited, intensive support, which is important to help parents overcome their challenges in providing a safe and nurturing environment for their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This will include counselling, improving parenting capacity and family functioning.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will also connect them to the community resources if they need additional support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We all know that more and more Singaporeans have caregiving responsibilities, not just for young children, but also for the elderly, the ill and the disabled among us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Chen Show Mao asked about what we can and ought to do to support such informal caregivers and enhance caregiving.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We all acknowledge that the family must continue to be the first line of support in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The question is: how best to support them?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is heartening that in Singapore's case, we have a report on Ageing Families in Singapore that was released in November last year which showed that close to nine in 10 elderly residents expressed confidence that they were able to rely on their children for financial support in times of emergency.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But what about those without children and those who are single?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: With shrinking family sizes, the role of the extended family becomes even more important.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I hope those of us with single or childless uncles and aunts will begin to think about how we ought to also consider our Page: 109 responsibilities to them as they age.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Today, various Government policies in housing, CPF, healthcare and the employment of foreign domestic workers already help immediate families care for their loved ones.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mr Chairman, I have located our Ministry's spending within a larger idea of what Singapore is, and of what the Singaporean is.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Even as we spend on our economy, defence, housing and healthcare, we know the key ingredient that makes our country special is our people.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our social spending contributes towards making Singapore our home.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It helps us build strong families and give every child a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will foster social mobility and we will give additional support to children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Equal opportunities, strong families, a united country – these are our enduring Singaporean values that will guide us in all that we do.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   Strong families are the basic building blocks of society and strong marriages form the foundation for strong families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With strong families and good support from society, our children can have a good start in life.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In MSF, we aspire to make Singapore Our Home for Family, where every child will have a good start in life.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We prioritise the strengthening of marriages and families through various educational programmes and support for marriage and parenthood.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will help couples to make adjustments when they enter married life and parenthood.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For couples who have divorced, we will help them to learn how to undertake co-parenting effectively.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As for their children, we will help them cope with adversity and help to increase their resilience.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, divorce rates involving Muslim couples who have recently married have shown a downward trend.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also received positive feedback about the changes and new programmes introduced for couples who are contemplating or undergoing divorce.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to expand and improve our educational programmes and support for marriage and parenthood.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One of our other main efforts is the support for young children and their parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue efforts to ensure that parents and children are able to access quality childcare and kindergartens.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Senior Minister of State Mrs Josephine Teo will also announce several enhancements to the leave scheme for parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am sure that many couples who will be embarking on their parenthood journey will welcome these initiatives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Page: 110 We agree that children from vulnerable groups will require more help.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This new initiative will proactively identify low-income and vulnerable children aged six and below.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It will provide them with access to health, learning and developmental support and monitor their progress during their early years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also provide parents with the knowledge and skills to care for and support their children's development.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Several Members have voiced their concern about the support provided to unwed parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the moment, support for unwed parents is already available, especially for the low-income, for example, childcare subsidies and financial assistance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MSF has carefully reviewed what other types of support can be provided to children of unwed parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will be implemented as soon as we amend the legislation and carry out system enhancements.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These benefits are most useful in the child's developmental or caregiving needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They will also support the unwed parents' efforts to provide for their children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, the extension of these benefits to unwed parents does not undermine parenthood within marriage, which is the prevalent social norm that has already been accepted and is highly valued by our society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These reasons are the basis for our decision.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope to work even more closely with the community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: All of us can have a role to play, especially in reaching out to families and children who require support and assistance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We can connect them to the available schemes of assistance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We can also help them in our personal capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We can spend time as volunteers for the Voluntary Welfare Organisations, as well as self-help groups, to help these families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together, we can make Singapore Our Home for Family, where every child will have a good start.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Sir, over the past few years, MSF has strengthened social assistance policies and delivery to better serve those in need.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This was not just about increasing the level and range of assistance available.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It was also about how our touch-points and officers could deliver help more flexibly and effectively.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are also making greater efforts to link up different help services to better serve families with complex needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Page: 111 Mr Amrin Amin asked about the effectiveness of SSOs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since we started developing the network three years ago, we have improved the accessibility and delivery of help.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, some nine in 10 SSO beneficiaries living in HDB towns can access an SSO within two kilometres of where they live or work.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With better accessibility, the SSOs have also helped more Singaporeans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A recent 2015 MSF survey showed that nine in 10 SSO users were satisfied with the service, regardless of whether they eventually received financial assistance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to improve the effectiveness and impact of the SSOs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They will take on a larger role in coordinating service delivery for families with more complex financial and social needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At Taman Jurong and Kreta Ayer, we are experimenting with bringing together social assistance, family services and employment services under one roof at the SSOs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Elsewhere, SSOs will actively coordinate with Government and community partners to integrate help, particularly in the areas of employment, family services, housing and healthcare.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Amrin was concerned that the tight labour supply will affect our ability to deliver help services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is a challenge faced by the social sector and, indeed, all other sectors in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will do more with our partners to uplift image, professional development and career prospects in the sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our officers also need support to do their job well.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I, therefore, thank Mr Amrin for raising concerns about the abuse of frontline SSO officers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some of our SSOs have security officers deployed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to take steps to protect our officers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will not hesitate to bring the perpetrators to task under the law, as we have done on a few occasions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One strategy to tackle the manpower challenge is to be more productive and coordinated in how we deliver services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This was why we decided to develop SSNet.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With this electronic backbone, we can share information and streamline work processes which will, in turn, reduce the administrative burden on both our beneficiaries and officers and improve the efficiency and quality of case management.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the progress of the implementation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are now addressing the teething problems and making improvements.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have also started planning for the next phase, to extend the system to other social services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The ComCare Long Term Assistance scheme, also commonly known as the Public Assistance (PA), provides a package of assistance to persons who are unable to work, with no means of income and limited or no family support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Page: 112 The package of help includes, firstly, cash assistance to meet basic living expenses; second, additional assistance where necessary for other recurring expenses like medical consumables and one-off purchases, such as household appliances; third, free medical treatment at polyclinics and public hospitals; and, lastly, befriending and social services in the community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many of the PA households are also allocated heavily subsidised HDB rental flats.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is to keep pace with the cost of living.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: ComCare also provides short- and medium- term assistance to low-income families and children in need.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our approach is to provide appropriate assistance to meet each family's needs and work with them so that, where possible, they can improve their lives and regain self-reliance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To answer Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin's concerns, besides financial needs, we also look at their food, shelter, caregiving, employment, family support and healthcare needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our SSOs would typically work with them to formulate action plans to guide them towards improving their circumstances in the different areas.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Such assistance is also available to foreign spouses in vulnerable transnational families, a point raised by Mr Ang Hin Kee.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, SSOs work with the Singapore Workforce Development Agency to help train ComCare recipients and place them in employment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SSOs may also link them up with financial literacy classes for proper budgeting, or with other social services if they have family or socio-emotional issues.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: CPF and HDB do give advice when home owners buy or sell their flats.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chen Show Mao and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh had asked about this.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: An example of a person or family who have graduated is the case of a male Singaporean aged 37 who approached the SSO in Chua Chu Kang in September 2014.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: He was also the sole breadwinner for the family and was not on full-time employment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: He and his spouse have three young children, youngest being two years old.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We provided the necessary assistance to the family.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together with our partners, we helped him secure a full-time job with a basic income of $1,800 a month in September 2015.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our assistance ended in September 2015 as the family was able to cope with their lives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, given the complexity of cases and variety of needs, there is no single definition of graduation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked if agencies can adopt a consistent definition of "income" in the criteria for different schemes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government has been making efforts to streamline income criteria and simplify processes where appropriate and we will continue to do so across schemes that target similar groups.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, MOH's subsidy schemes for outpatient and long-term care and MSF's residential subsidy schemes for adults with disabilities make use of a common set of income information.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, there are also schemes that focus on fairly unique beneficiary groups or needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is more appropriate for these to adopt different income bases.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to partner other Government agencies to review this, so as to make our assistance schemes more citizen-centric.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some vulnerable adults may not be able to care for themselves and may lack family support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our social workers, especially those from the family violence Page: 113 specialist centres, have given us useful feedback for the Bill.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are also caregivers who are themselves elderly and face the real concern of loss of mental capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We appreciate the public feedback and suggestions raised by Members, such as Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Seah Kian Peng, that have helped us streamline the application process for the Lasting Power of Attorney and the appointment of deputies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Ms Rahayu Mahzam has pointed out, we have also come across some seniors who are unable to provide for themselves and are unable to receive financial support from their children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Maintenance of Parents Act provides a legal recourse for these elderly to claim maintenance from their children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Act was amended in 2011 to strengthen its conciliatory aspects.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If mediation is unsuccessful, the Tribunal may, as a last resort, make a maintenance order if it considers it just and equitable for the children to maintain their elderly parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Where the children themselves may be struggling financially, the elderly parents are referred to the SSOs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The elderly can also turn to the SSOs on their own.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our officers will assess the case and work closely with partners, such as FSCs, to reconcile the family and provide assistance to the elderly.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From the elderly, let me now turn to youth-at-risk.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MSF already funds youth-at-risk programmes to ensure that youths have opportunities to be meaningfully engaged and not go off onto the wrong path.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through these, we aim to improve the quality and consistency of service delivery for our programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We plan to provide booster grants to help appointed agencies develop their organisational capability and train youth workers to become more competent in managing youths with varying levels of risk.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These enhancements will support our programmes to deliver better outcomes for youths-at-risk.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are now in our final year of the second Enabling Masterplan.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MSF, together with various Ministries and VWOs, have brought about substantial progress under this second Masterplan.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have prepared a booklet that summarises how the support for persons with disabilities across their life stages and how their quality of life have improved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This booklet will also be made available on MSF's website.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As the booklet is fairly comprehensive, I will just highlight a few areas of progress and share some new initiatives and improvements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: First is in the area of training and employment, key enablers to help persons with disabilities lead independent lives and realise their potential.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong asked about the efficacy of the Open Door Job Portal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The job portal is part of the Open Door Programme launched in April 2014 to support employers in hiring and integrating persons with disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SG Enable, an agency set up by the Ministry to enhance employability and employment options for persons with disabilities, is working closely with employers to further raise awareness.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Recently, I met some employers at the Enabling Village and was impressed by Uniqlo's commitment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They aim to hire at least one person with disability in each of their Singapore stores.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, they hired over 40 persons with disabilities in 2015.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I believe we can help even more persons with disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will expand efforts to support the hiring of persons with disabilities in the public sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will identify job opportunities, especially where their skills sets and disposition give them an advantage and, where needed, redesign work processes and improve workplace accessibility.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I know many caregivers are concerned about the accessibility of adult care services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the last five years, we have increased the capacity of Day Activity Centres by 40% to 1,200 places in 2015.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: By 2018, we will add another 600 places.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Half of these new places will cater to the rising number of adults with autism.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: From April 2016, we will vary our funding support in these centres based on level of needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This means that those with more severe needs will be given more Government support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will also equip service providers with skills to better manage clients with challenging behaviours.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Chia asked about end-of-life issues and whether the Government can help parents and caregivers with permanency planning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is, indeed, a concern amongst the many parents we speak to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is also why my Ministry had set up the Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SNTC works with caregivers to develop care plans and set up Trust accounts to ensure that the long-term financial and care support of persons with disabilities are met.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Three hundred and ninety families have benefited thus far.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Parents can also nominate their children to receive monthly disbursements from their CPF savings after their demise, through the Special Needs Saving Scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will also look into building up the capability of social workers and other professional staff working with persons with disabilities, to better support long-term care planning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Third, I should cite our efforts to raise public awareness and celebrate the achievements of persons with disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The ASEAN Para Games was a milestone event that showcased the abilities of our para-athletes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Team Singapore fielded 156 athletes in 15 sports.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Many of us who watched the events were inspired by their spirit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am proud of how Page: 115 well our para-athletes did, winning medals in 10 sports.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Games' impact goes way beyond the week of competition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth and SPORT Singapore are now working with MSF to increase accessibility to sports for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are many more areas – in healthcare insurance coverage, education, transport and built environment, in support of the use of technology and improving sector capability – where we have made progress over the past five years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Seah asked about the Assistive Technology Fund take-up since it was enhanced in August last year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the past seven months, more than 500 persons with disabilities have benefited from the enhanced funding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is five times more than in the past.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With the Enabling Masterplan 2 in its final year, we have started work to develop the next Enabling Masterplan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This will guide the development of policies, programmes, services and other support for persons with disabilities from 2017 onwards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have formed a steering committee that will develop this plan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It has 22 members from the people, private and public sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Seah has asked what the Masterplan will focus on.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: My Ministry and partners are holding a series of focus group discussions as part of the SG Future series.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I hope that every one of us will take part in this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The important role that Singaporeans play in this cannot be overstated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Occasionally, we hear of indiscriminate use of wheelchair accessible parking lots at the expense of persons who Page: 116 need them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We hear about onlookers' lack of understanding when a person with autism is having a meltdown in public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As Ms Chia had so eloquently put it last week, there are disabilities that are real even if they are not visible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We need every part of our society to understand, be considerate and help support the integration of persons with disabilities in everyday life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Likewise, to effectively help the low-income, vulnerable elderly, at-risk youth and other groups with less, we will need the support of everyone in our community to identify who may need help, to reach out and understand what they are going through and what they need and to render support − big or small.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Building a caring and inclusive society requires all Singaporeans to play a part.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to start, if I may, with a continuation of the earlier ideas about the Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In the first part of my speech, I spoke about Singaporeans, the strengths of our beliefs in key values of equal opportunities, strong families and a united country and how we design our policies around these key ideas.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But of the last, we believe that unity exists when we have a people that care for one another.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Caring communities are characterised by people with: firstly, awareness – which is the head − recognising that there are those among us who are disadvantaged, who are vulnerable; secondly, empathy − our heart − tying ourselves to our countrymen, recognising where they are in life and what they may need; and, lastly, action – our hands – contributing in practical ways to make lives better, to make things easier for them, lending them a helping hand to live their lives well and with dignity.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Many Members in this debate have spoken on the need for the community to be involved.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: When a Singaporean in need receives help from a fellow citizen, he knows that someone else out there cares for him.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In the process of helping others, those who lend a hand are themselves transformed.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, in the act of mutual help, we become more than ourselves and our immediate families.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We become a better people, a closer community, we become a united country.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: VWOs and social service professionals are really at the forefront of this.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And the social sector really is the vehicle for change.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: VWOs and social service professionals will continue to be key in helping people overcome their difficulties.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They work with and complement the role of the Government.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They are also indispensable in generating awareness, fostering empathy and channelling the contributions of our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, I expect many and encourage volunteers to continue to come through the VWOs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But the reality is that each of us can also put these values into action in our own ways − as concerned neighbours or friends, as volunteers and participants in schools and informal groups, as socially responsible companies or inclusive employers, or simply as an individual.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These are things we can do and we do not need legislation or policies to make it happen.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In the coming year, MSF will have three priorities: firstly, support VWOs to raise their capability and provide better volunteering opportunities and experiences; secondly, help social service professionals develop themselves through SkillsFuture; and, thirdly, work with the wider community towards these ends.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will find more ways to encourage companies and other groups to form meaningful and complementary partnerships with VWOs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Page: 117 Mr Chairman, our VWOs need to be strong and they need to be healthy.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Against the landscape of an ageing population and slowing labour growth, our VWOs need to be adept and nimble to be able to do more; to attract, develop and retain good people; and to marshal and mobilise resources well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng and Ms Chia Yong Yong asked about support for VWOs as they build up their corporate functions and their operational capabilities.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are making significant investments in these areas.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For VWOs that can scale up services, the Government has also provided additional funding for them to hire senior corporate staff under the Corporate Development Funding Scheme.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, funding is available through various sources and grant schemes.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But I agree with Ms Chia Yong Yong that we should also regularly review scheme criteria and improve the grant application process.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Later this year, NCSS will also centralise the information on grants and schemes for VWOs on their website.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They will make it easier for VWOs to understand and navigate the range of grants available.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In fact, it is a happy problem that we have so many grants that we cannot figure out which grants are applicable and relevant.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But grant administrators will continue to advise and guide VWOs on their application and streamline the processes.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Besides providing resources, we will also help VWOs tap on external experts and consultants.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This will help the VWOs diagnose needs and improve their HR capabilities in recruitment, compensation and benefits, performance management and career planning.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan asked about the manpower supply outlook.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Government and NCSS will continue to plan the supply pipelines and training places and NCSS' career centre will continue to help VWOs source for suitable candidates.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But how well VWOs cope with tight manpower will also depend on how they strengthen their organisational capabilities, innovate and deploy resources.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I hope VWOs will make full use of some of the schemes that I have just mentioned.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about how we are investing in and supporting the professionals in the social service and early childhood sectors.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan also asked about how we will help the sector cope with competition for manpower.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We intend to make a strong push in tapping on SkillsFuture.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These plans will map out ways in which professionals and organisations can acquire skills and capabilities to meet evolving social challenges in a manpower-lean future.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The plans will also look at how our sectors can close existing skills gaps and develop new skills that professionals will need in the future; how do we utilise manpower better and work in a manpower-efficient way, similar to Page: 118 what is needed in the private sector as well; and map out career progression and professional development opportunities for professionals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Members will include professionals, VWOs and preschool operators and unions.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They will be our key partners in bringing these plans to fruition.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Chairman, a strong social service sector needs the support of the wider community and the public.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It needs organisations and individuals to volunteer and contribute their time, skills and resources.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To expand volunteering opportunities and experiences, NCSS will provide more support to VWOs in building up volunteer management capabilities.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Recently, for example, NCSS started a pilot with Care Corner and Thye Hua Kwan Moral Charities to redesign jobs in a youth centre and a Senior Activity Centre respectively to better tap on volunteers to complement the centres' staff.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I have asked NCSS to expand such efforts and make a stronger push in this important area.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Minister for Finance spoke about boosting Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and making it easier for employees to contribute through their workplaces.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are a few reasons why SHARE is so significant and impactful.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Every Singaporean and every organisation can contribute regularly, even in modest amounts, through SHARE.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The donations go to a pool that supports a big group of 80 VWOs, including smaller VWOs that lack the scale to fund-raise effectively.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They also support lesser-known programmes that may not attract sizeable donations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: A large part of SHARE contributions come through payroll deductions at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: One SHARE donor, Mr Abraham Tan, started donating $1 from his monthly pay 20 years ago when he was earning $500.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As his pay increased, he raised his monthly contribution.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Tan told us: "Everyone should play a part if we want to live in a caring society.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The little that we contribute may help another to achieve their dream".

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Every additional dollar, if all of us participate, makes a tremendous amount of difference if it is regular.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will allow half of the matching grant, up to a cap of $10,000 per year, to support SHARE participating companies with their CSR efforts.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And the rest will be used to help VWOs improve their volunteer management.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Chairman, I would like to end off by reiterating that MSF's efforts contribute towards our goal of building the society that we aspire to be – a land of opportunity where citizens can realise their dreams, with equal opportunities, strong families and a united country.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Page: 119 Members of the House, what I have presented to you today started a decade ago to improve the way we provide help to the weaker among us, to provide this help with respect for the dignity of those who need it; not treat them with suspicion, that they may be free riding, not make it hard to get help with bureaucratic hoops and hurdles; and even as we promote a strong work ethic and social mobility, we have in this time recognised that all of us have the same place in society.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Weak or strong, fast or slow, we are all sons and daughters of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And, together, we are only as strong as the values we hold dear.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Our Government will continue to make help systems more comprehensive and effective, but it is not about the number of programmes we churn out, or the amount of money we spend, or even the number of people we help.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is not about what the Government can do, or what the community can get the Government to do.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is about how we, as a small country, can make us count for more as a nation than all of us as individuals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is the true Spirit of Partnership, the spirit that the Minister for Finance mentioned in his Budget speech.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The spirit that will show us how we can, together, create the society that we wish to see 50 years from now, for SG100.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have time for a few clarifications before we start our debate for the next Ministry.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: First, I want to thank the Minister for his very strong support and for his strong advocate for fathers to be active.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: For divorced families, however, I think this can be quite challenging when the father does not live with or does not see the children often.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Minister, what can we do for this group of fathers?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: My second clarification is for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Indeed, there has been much progress that has been made to make Singapore more inclusive for people with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How we treat people with disabilities is important because they are a cornerstone in building an inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I would appreciate clarifications on these two points.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister Tan, can you keep the reply short?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Chairman, clearly, the role of fathers is important, especially in divorce.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Children growing up under those circumstances do face a lot of challenges.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But I think the responsibilities of fathers do not change.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is where, in terms of the support programmes we have put in place, are to help the parents themselves.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The relationship may have soured but we want them to understand the continued impact that they can have on their children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Hopefully, through these programmes, they begin to understand how they can continue to carve out roles for themselves – even though in a divorced state – that each of them can continue carrying out their responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Page: 120 Ultimately, it is very important for the individuals to want to put in that effort.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will do what we can to support it but, like many of our policies, the very last mile needs to be walked by the individuals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will do our utmost best to support them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am very happy that many organisations and individuals have played a part in increasing the awareness of this sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For example, in 2015, NCSS carried out two public education efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The other effort is being socially enabled, that relates closer to the ASEAN Para Games.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The NCSS is working closely with people with disabilities, as well as the public, as to how we can do a baseline study and also have a multi-pronged effort in public education in the years to come.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have said earlier, we are fortunate to have partners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If you look around this month, you will see structures and also buildings going blue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is a symbol of the autism movement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Buildings like the National Gallery, Helix Bridge, Khoo Teck Puat Hospital and St Andrew's Cathedral.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What we have seen is that we have done a lot as a society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the words of my Minister in the Enabling Masterplan 2 progress report, he said, "The direction is clear and there is no turning back.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will keep up the momentum." So, we will do more together as a society.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: I have two clarifications, the first for the Minister and the second for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: Will there be a policy differentiation and whether that will be reflected in any ensuing legislative change?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: Second clarification, Sir, will be for the Parliamentary Secretary who mentioned the special needs savings scheme.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: I understand this scheme applies only to parents of children with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: It does not apply to caregivers of charges with disabilities, so will that be extended?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: In my cut, I was referring to permanency planning which extends beyond financial provision to other caregiving options, so could the Ministry also be looking further into broadening the scope?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For the first question, we will take it back.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These are the things that we will continue to improve on as we move along.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Regarding the Minister's desire to promote a caring community and to empower volunteers to step in and to devote their time and resources, I would like to clarify for community-initiated programmes to provide informal childcare services, will the Ministry be able to provide some broad-based guidelines so that safety considerations can be addressed in such informal arrangements?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Chairman, we do endeavour to provide as best support as possible to parents.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do recognise, especially at the infant stage, that it is challenging because it is very labour-intensive.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do also recognise that many different groups are exploring the possibility of informal arrangements.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are in the midst of exploring what are the various possibilities, so if there are community groups that have ground-up initiatives, do let us know and we can take a look at how we can extend support if possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are also working our way around this together with NPTD in terms of how best to approach this particular space.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Has the Ministry given any thought in relation to KidSTART that since the children will be proactively identified by the ECDA, what will you do in cases where parents are reluctant to release their children to take part in these activities or are even resistant to co-operate with the programme?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Chairman, that is an important question because, as I have mentioned, in many of these various initiatives, whether it is KidSTART or in other ideas in terms of supporting families and individuals, it really does depend on the individual responding.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do know from our experience that not every individual responds.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The children are usually innocent in the process.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Parents, sometimes, may not be very cooperative for a host of reasons.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We endeavour to try to understand, which is why a lot of this work is very, very labour-intensive.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some of the work that we do is almost one-to-one.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some of our social workers are spending almost sometimes five to seven days a week on the job, because they are not only just spending time with the child, they are spending time with the family.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As I have mentioned earlier, we do recognise, philosophically, it is always best to be with the birth family even though it may be imperfect.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are circumstances that we take children away as well and that is why fostering becomes important.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is why institutional care, sometimes, also becomes important.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is frightfully difficult and very emotive, but it is something we are struggling with.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is a very difficult area of work for our officers but we are working very closely to see how best to address this.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Where parents are not cooperative, we will work with them to, hopefully, turn them round.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Many advanced countries have a clear definition of graduation from relative poverty because they have a relative poverty line and they check the progress of their welfare schemes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
