text: Does the Ministry track how many beneficiaries become self-reliant at the end of the assistance?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have said earlier in my answer, realistically, due to the complexity of the cases and the different needs, you realise that each individual and family's graduation refers to different forms of graduation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Our approach is actually to uplift everyone, whether someone is poor or in need of help, to better their lives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As Members of Parliament, we have come across many cases whereby we have helped them and seen their lives improve, day after day.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, if you go back to the notion of having a clear, clean definition, you realise it does not work that way on the ground.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am very passionate about this because, to me, what is important is that each and every one of us plays a part.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are all touchpoints of the people around us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If you see any of them having difficulties, be it financially or socially, please find ways to get them to the SSOs for help.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If you cannot find where the SSOs are, remember this number: 1800 222 0000.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am very serious here because when it comes to issues like these, it means a lot to our residents who need help.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to have one clarification on KidSTART.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: If there are particular cases that Dr Lily Neo would like to raise for consideration, we will take a look at them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It does not preclude the whole series of different outreach efforts that we have that are already on-going.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: If I may also add, we do not have one definition of poverty per se and many of us encounter them in many, many different circumstances.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: If you use the analogy of social safety nets, what we have is a series of safety nets at different levels for different groups.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What you want to make sure is, within each net, it is interwoven enough so that it is tight.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And between the nets, you make sure that the gaps are not there.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And especially, using the analogy of a trampoline, these nets are also to help you to be able to stand.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Page: 123 In the cases where they fall outside of that particular definition of, say, aged six and below, we will look at them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: If there are needs, I think we will endeavour to see how best to address those needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Chairman, I have a clarification for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I had earlier highlighted the situation where elderly parents refuse to claim from their children if they need assistance.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: What is the Ministry's position or approach with regard to this matter and what more can we do to help this group of elderly citizens?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, we understand there are parents who are elderly who do not want to go through the system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will look at the scenarios and the circumstances that the family and the elderly face.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And we will also see how the community network can be part of it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have strong community networks in Singapore and this is an area where we can help them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I have met cases like that in my area where, sometimes, we think that they need help.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I asked them and they tell me, "No, I am happy, I do not need help".

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What I do is I get my community volunteers to come and partner them and be part of the process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we keep a look-out for them, so that they do not really fall into whatever difficulties.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I have a short clarification for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Earlier, he mentioned that ECDA will work with SSO for families with vulnerable children.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: My question relates to children in the care of a foreign spouse due to the Singaporean spouse either passing away or in a state of divorce or in prison.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Will ECDA also work with ICA and MOM on employment opportunities and long-term staying rights for this foreign spouse?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: I want to credit the Ministry for the tremendous effort made in providing childcare services for the residents.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As we increase the number of places in terms of capacity in the schools, we do need to recruit more teachers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have put in place a wide range of initiatives.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The response has been positive thus far, but we are tracking it very closely.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: If, for whatever reason, the response is not as strong as we would like it to be, we do have various levers to adjust and to make sure that we will be on track to meet the demands of the people in order to make sure that their children are educated.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, without speeches, would you want to consider withdrawing your amendment?

text: On behalf of all Members, I want to thank the Minister, Parliamentary Secretary, Permanent Secretary Mr Chan Heng Kee and his team at MSF and also all the social service professionals, workers and volunteers for ensuring that the heart-beat of our country remains one which is strong, compassionate, caring and assuring to all Singaporeans.
